--- title: "Accessible Jobs (ATO City Rollup)" subtitle: "Scoping document — City x City detail script runs successfully against real Cube Voyager" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 embed-resources: true execute: echo: false warning: false message: false jupyter: july2025 --- **[← All run sets](../../index.qmd)** ## The question WFRC wants a new web app showing where accessible jobs are, in the same desire-line/arc style as `APP-WFRC-Commute-Patterns` — a separate, existing repo that maps *observed* LEHD commute flows as curved arcs between cities, sized by worker counts. The new app would show a *modeled* quantity instead: for a selected city, how many jobs its residents can reach, split into - **Internal** — jobs within the city, accessible from within the city - **Outbound** — jobs *outside* the city that the city's own residents can reach - **Inbound** — how much the city's own jobs contribute to *other* cities' accessibility The TDM already computes a decay-weighted **Access to Opportunity (ATO)** index per zone. The gap isn't the underlying model — it's that today's ATO output collapses every destination into a single number per origin, with no way to tell *which* destinations it came from, which is what a city rollup needs. ## Decisions already made - **City assignment uses the TAZ shapefile's own city field, not Census/TIGER place boundaries.** `APP-WFRC-Commute-Patterns` defines "city" via Census places; the TDM's `WFv1000_TAZ.dbf` has its own `CITY_UGRC` field. No reconciliation between the two is planned — the rollup uses `CITY_UGRC` directly, matching the field `bring-work-trips-closer-to-home` already uses for its "City Area" geography. - **The TAZ-to-city aggregation happens inside the Cube script, not in Python afterward** (Option A below) — chosen over emitting a large thresholded TAZ-pair file and aggregating downstream, because the city set is small enough that the in-script approach produces a tiny output directly, with no cutoff-tuning needed. - **Custom code lives in this run set's own folder, never inside `tdm/`** — same principle as every other run set's custom driver scripts (see `docs/architecture/0007-custom-driver-script.md`): a new Cube script and a small crosswalk file go in `run_sets/accessible-jobs-ato/scripts/` and `run_sets/accessible-jobs-ato/inputs/`, never as an edit to `tdm/2_ModelScripts/`. ## Decisions still needed | Decision | Options | Recommendation | If left unresolved | |---|---|---|---| | **Decay-weighted index vs. a literal job count** | Ship only the existing decay-weighted ATO units (continuous, not a hard travel-time cutoff) rolled up by city; or additionally compute a parallel hard-cutoff variant ("jobs within 30 minutes") | Ship the decay-weighted rollup first — it's the TDM's existing, validated measure, reuses the same `ATO_Weight.csv` decay curve already in production use. Add a hard-cutoff variant later if a public-facing "X jobs within Y minutes" framing turns out to matter more than the index | Defaults to decay-weighted only; a literal job-count headline number isn't available for the app | | **Sector detail in v1** | Roll up `SE_File.dbf`'s job categories (`RETEMP`/`INDEMP`/`OTHEMP`, or finer) alongside the total, so the app can show an industry mix of *accessible* jobs; or defer to a later pass | Include it now — the script already visits zone `j`'s `SE_File` row once per pair; carrying a few more fields costs nothing extra | Defaults to total jobs only; no industry-mix chart possible in the app's first version | | **Reverse "workers accessible" quantity** | Compute the HH-weighted mirror image (how many workers can reach this city's jobs) alongside the jobs-weighted version now, or later | Include it now — same reasoning as sector detail, the loop already visits every pair once | Defaults to the jobs-accessible direction only | : {tbl-colwidths="[28,32,25,15]" .fixed-table} ## What the model already gives us to work with ::: {#baseline-table .cell execution_count=2} These numbers are real, pulled from an already-completed model run — the existing `Access_to_Opportunity.csv` from the region's converged 2023 base network, curated into this run set via `import-manual-run` with no new Cube Voyager run. | Metric | Value | |---|---:| | TAZs with a row in today's output | 3,562 | | Total households across those TAZs | 885,096 | | Total jobs across those TAZs | 1,713,932 | | Mean per-TAZ decay-weighted ATO (jobs, auto) | 329,361 | | Mean per-TAZ decay-weighted ATO (jobs, transit) | 52,247 | | Mean per-TAZ decay-weighted ATO (jobs, bike) | 68,978 | | Mean per-TAZ decay-weighted ATO (jobs, walk) | 3,938 | ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Correction to an earlier assumption, checked against real output Today's `08_Access_to_Opportunity.s` gates its output row on `DEVACRES>0` (a developable-acreage field, likely there to feed WFRC's REMM land-use model). Earlier discussion flagged this as a risk — that non-developable TAZs would be silently missing from a rollup. Checked against the real curated file above: **all 3,562 real TAZs get a row** (the TDM's `UsedZones=3629` includes ~67 external/dummy zones that are already excluded by the script's own zone loop, unrelated to `DEVACRES`). So this filter isn't dropping any real zone in the current base scenario. It's still the right call for the new script not to inherit this filter — a fully built-out TAZ in a different scenario or vintage could plausibly have `DEVACRES=0` — but it is not an active bug in today's data, and shouldn't be described as one. ::: | Need | Existing TDM piece | Status | |---|---|---| | Decay-weighted accessibility by mode, per zone | `tdm/2_ModelScripts/5_AssignHwy/08_Access_to_Opportunity.s` | Exists, real, in production — computes exactly this for auto (congested/free-flow/straight-line), transit (walk- and drive-access, peak only), bike, and walk. The gap is that it only ever writes the *collapsed* per-origin total — no row for any individual destination pair exists on disk today | | Jobs and households by TAZ | `SE_File.dbf` (`TOTHH`/`TOTEMP`, plus sector detail) | Exists in every scenario folder already | | Travel-time skims by mode | Highway (`Skm_AM/PM/FF.mtx`) and transit (`skm_w4-9_Pk.mtx`/`skm_d4-9_Pk.mtx`) | Exist in every scenario folder already; transit skims are peak-only, so a time-of-day comparison is only possible for auto today | | TAZ-to-city assignment, TAZ centroids | `tdm/1_Inputs/1_TAZ/WFv1000_TAZ.dbf` | Already has `CITY_FIPS`/`CITY_UGRC`/`CITY_NAME`, county, the full small/medium/large/super planning-district hierarchy, and `X`/`Y` centroids as static per-TAZ attributes — confirmed by reading the field list directly. No new export needed; the app's data pipeline reads this live from `tdm/`, the same way `non-motorized-2023`'s reports already read TAZ/district shapefiles live rather than curating a copy | | A converged base scenario to compute against | `v10.0-beta.2`'s `v10.0-beta.2-2023` scenario | Already run and registered here as this run set's `base` scenario, same reuse `household-location-burden` already does — no new full model run needed | : {tbl-colwidths="[30,40,30]" .fixed-table} ## Proposed design: Option A — aggregate to city inside the Cube script `08_Access_to_Opportunity.s` already loops over every `(i, j)` TAZ pair — that's how it computes the collapsed per-origin total today. The new script (`run_sets/accessible-jobs-ato/scripts/access_to_opportunity_detail.s`, a sibling of the original, not an edit to it) reuses that same loop structure but accumulates into a **City × City array** instead of a per-origin scalar, using a `TAZID → CityIdx` crosswalk to decide which city cell a pair's decayed contribution belongs in. This now runs successfully end to end — see "Effort and runtime" below for the real debugging path that got there, including two abandoned designs (a `LOOKUP`-based text translation, then a `CITY_FIPS`-based one) and the fact that the array itself has to be flattened to one dimension, not the genuine 2D array first assumed. ```{mermaid} flowchart LR Skims["Skims + SE_File
(already exist per scenario)"] --> Loop["Per-(i,j) TAZ loop
(existing script structure, reused)"] CityIdx["city_index.csv
TAZID -> CityIdx, loaded as DBI"] --> Loop Loop --> Array["Flattened City x City array
CityFlat = (City_i-1)*82+City_j"] Array --> Output["New output file:
one row per city pair, per mode"] Output --> Rollup["App rollup:
diagonal = Internal
row = Outbound, column = Inbound"] ``` Why this table already gives you Internal/Outbound/Inbound for free: the diagonal of a `(home_city, work_city)` table is Internal; reading across a city's own row (excluding the diagonal) is Outbound; reading down its own column (excluding the diagonal) is Inbound. This is the identical shape `APP-WFRC-Commute-Patterns`'s own `aggregate_city_flows()` already produces for LODES data, and the same self-flow-exclusion query pattern its `db.js` already uses (`IS DISTINCT FROM`, not `!=`, for the same reason: some geographies leave the column `NULL` rather than empty). **How it actually gets run — a second scenario, seeded by `start_from_copy`, not a manual invocation against the shared folder.** An earlier draft of this plan proposed running the new script directly against `base`'s raw folder (`v10.0-beta.2-2023`) — rejected, since that folder is shared: `household-location-burden`'s own `base` scenario also points at it via `manual_scenario_folder`, and mutating it with an untested new script risks that run set's bookkeeping too. Instead, this run set declares a second scenario, **`city-detail`** (`run_sets/accessible-jobs-ato/scenarios/city-detail.yaml`), with `start_from_copy: base` — the framework's existing seeding mechanism (see CLAUDE.md's `start_from_copy` architecture note) that copies a sibling scenario's *entire* raw folder into this scenario's own, before running anything. `city-detail` runs through the normal CLI (`tdmruns run-scenario`), using a minimal custom `driver_script` (`run_sets/accessible-jobs-ato/hail-mary/__HailMary_1Subfolder_ato_detail.s`) that reads only `_ControlCenter.block` and `GeneralParameters.block` (the same two files every driver script reads first) and then `access_to_opportunity_detail.s` — none of the actual model pipeline steps. Since `base`'s folder is 34 GB, this copy is the expensive part of running this scenario at all, not the new script itself; `city-detail.yaml` now declares `lock_down_copy: true` (added after the first successful copy) so later retries (while debugging the new script) don't repeat that copy. Its output then gets added to `run_set.yaml`'s `outputs.include` and picked up by `tdmruns import-manual-run` or the run's own automatic curation, exactly like the existing collapsed file already curated for this run set (see the table above). ## Known limitations, carried into the app regardless of the rollup design - **Transit is peak-only.** Every transit skim file is named `_Pk` — there's no off-peak transit skim, so "accessible jobs by time of day" can only vary for auto today. - **Auto's Internal/Outbound split will likely skew heavily toward Outbound** — auto's decay radius typically exceeds a single city's diameter, so most of a city's *own* jobs are barely decayed at all and the split is more informative for walk/bike/transit. - **No sector taxonomy match to the companion app's LODES-based industry mix.** `SE_File.dbf`'s categories (`RETEMP`/`INDEMP`/`OTHEMP`, or the finer `RETL`/`MANU`/`OFFI`/etc.) are trip-generation categories, not LODES's NAICS-based supersectors — an industry-mix chart in the new app needs its own legend, not a relabeled copy of the commute app's. - **No age/earnings analog at all.** `SE_File.dbf` carries no wage-band or age split of jobs, so those two dimensions from the commute app have no TDM equivalent and would simply be absent from the accessible-jobs app. ## Effort and runtime No new full Cube Voyager model run was needed — the new script reads skims and `SE_File.dbf` that already exist in `city-detail`'s (seeded from `base`) scenario folder. Confirmed by an actual run (2026-09-07): **4.5 minutes** end to end, bounded by the same `(i, j)` TAZ-pair loop the existing collapsed script already pays for every scenario run today (roughly 3,600 × 3,600 ≈ 13 million pairs). **The script now runs successfully end to end.** Getting there took four real Cube Voyager compile failures, each fixed from the actual error message in `TPPL####.PRN`, not guessed in advance: 1. `LOOKUP` has no `STRING=T` option (`F(018): STRING is invalid key`) — text-keyed lookup isn't available the way it was first assumed to be. 2. The numeric fallback (`CITY_FIPS`, already on `WFv1000_TAZ.dbf`) turned out to have a real data collision, not a syntax problem: `CITY_FIPS=0` is shared by Hill AFB and unincorporated county land. 3. `ARRAY name = N` dimensions must be a literal integer — a variable (`NUM_CITIES`) compiled as `ARRAY ...=NUM_CITIES is invalid value`. 4. **The big one:** `ARRAY CityJob_Auto = 82, 82` does **not** declare a two-dimensional array in Cube MATRIX — it silently does the same thing `08_Access_to_Opportunity.s`'s own confirmed-working `ARRAY Node_X = N, Node_Y = N` does: declare two separate *one*-dimensional arrays. Every `[City_i, City_j]` two-subscript access failed with `F(160): City_j has incorrect number of subscripts`, regardless of how the subscript variables were declared. Fixed by flattening to a single dimension (`CityFlat = (City_i-1)*82 + City_j`, arrays sized `6724` literal) instead of continuing to guess at Cube's real multi-dimensional array syntax. Final design also reverted the crosswalk mechanism itself: rather than a `LOOKUP()`-based translation of `WFv1000_TAZ.dbf`'s `CITY_UGRC` (attempts 1 and 2 above), the working script reads a small **TAZID → CityIdx** file (`inputs/city_index.csv`) as a plain `DBI` with `DELIMITER=','` — the exact mechanism `1_DemographicsAnalysis.s` already uses for `WFRC_SEFile`/ `MAG_SEFile` — populated into a zone-indexed array via a `LOOP`, the same pattern already used for `Node_X`/`Node_Y`. This is a per-TAZ file again (the thing an earlier design pass deliberately avoided), but for a concrete, tested reason rather than a preference: `CITY_UGRC`/`CITY_FIPS` translation inside Cube didn't work. **Cross-validated against the trusted original script:** the new City × City table's grand total for `Job_Auto` (summed across all 6,724 city pairs) is **1,173,182,979** — within 0.002% of `3,562 × 329,361` (TAZ count times the existing collapsed script's own mean per-TAZ `Job_byAuto`, from the baseline table above). Both numbers sum the same underlying decayed-contribution terms, just aggregated differently, so this near-exact match is real evidence the new script's decay/travel-time math agrees with the original, not just that it compiled. Build order, updated to reflect what's actually done: 1. ✅ `scripts/build_city_index.py` builds `inputs/city_index.csv` (TAZID → CityIdx, 3,562 rows, 82 distinct cities) from `WFv1000_TAZ.dbf`. 2. ✅ `scripts/access_to_opportunity_detail.s` runs successfully against `city-detail` (seeded from `base` via `start_from_copy`), producing a sane City × City table — cross-checked against the baseline above. 3. ✅ `run_set.yaml`'s `outputs.include` picked up the new file automatically on the successful `run-scenario` invocation — both it and the existing collapsed file are curated under `runs/accessible-jobs-ato/city-detail/outputs/`. 4. **Not yet done.** Build the app-side query layer against the new curated file — this mirrors `db.js`'s `queryFlows`/`querySelfFlow` pattern in `APP-WFRC-Commute-Patterns` almost unchanged (diagonal = Internal, row = Outbound, column = Inbound). ## Bottom line The underlying model (ATO) already exists and is already in production use — this wasn't new modeling work, it was exposing destination-level detail that the original script computes and then throws away, and it now works, verified against real Cube Voyager output and cross-checked against the trusted baseline. The two open decisions above (decay-weighted-only vs. also adding a hard-cutoff job count; how much sector/reverse-direction detail ships in v1) still have working defaults. Remaining work is the app-side query layer, not the TDM side. ## Run history ::: {#run-history .cell execution_count=3} **TDM Version:** v10.0.0-beta.2
